scope: Prepares the deterministic standard-calibrated IQ2_XS artifact for private Hugging Face upload, splits it under the Hub per-file limit, verifies the split semantically, creates the destination repository and metadata, and records the private-storage blocker preventing shard upload.

artifact.classification: Static per-tensor GGUF requantization; not runtime dynamic quantization

hub_repository.metadata_roundtrip: PASS: downloaded README.md and manifest.json and compared them byte-for-byte

split.reason: Hugging Face rejected the single 62.08-GiB object with HTTP 422: max individual file size is 50.0 GB
split.tool: llama-gguf-split from the deterministic pinned build

split_verification.whole_file_result: Different from the unsharded source because GGUF split metadata and header alignment are reconstructed
split_verification.semantic_check: All 1,224 tensor names, shapes, types, expected byte counts, and payload SHA-256 values matched the unsharded source
split_verification.temporary_merge_cleanup: Removed the exact task-owned merge-verification file and directory

upload_blocker.attempt: Legacy multipart LFS batch upload for both verified shards
upload_blocker.hub_message: Private storage limit reached for user Kearm, please upgrade your plan to increase your private storage limit.
upload_blocker.credential_boundary: The Hugging Face token remained on the authenticated main machine; no account token was installed on Strix.
upload_blocker.required_user_action: Increase Kearm private Hub storage, or explicitly authorize a different private destination. Public upload is not permitted by the project policy.

non_claims: No GGUF shard bytes were uploaded because the Hub refused the private LFS upload before issuing transfer actions.
The exact private-storage quota numerator, denominator, and current billed usage were not exposed by the whoami response.
A llama.cpp split/merge is not byte-identical at the whole-file level; only the tensor-level equality above is claimed.
The model card records the one-token execution gate but makes no quality or general-throughput claim.
